nodes.statement: In a December 13, 2025 first-hand home review after three months using Posha, Jennifer Pattison Tuohy reported making dozens of dishes and leaving macaroni cheese cooking while she worked. The device dispensed, heated and stirred; she still chopped, weighed and loaded ingredients. Meals served one to four, took roughly 30–60 minutes and sometimes longer than manual cooking. The reviewed unit required internet, counter space and a subscription; quoted price was $1,500 plus about $15/month. This establishes household use of partial cooking automation, not universal availability, current pricing or population-wide time savings.

nodes.source_refs: ["https://www.fao.org/director-general/speeches/details/launch-of-the-state-of-food-security-and-nutrition-in-the-world-(sofi)-2026-report-statement/en | progress remains slow, uneven, and fragile | 2026-07-21"]
nodes.statement: FAO’s July 21, 2026 SOFI launch statement estimates 645 million people faced hunger in 2025 (7.8%), nearly 14 million fewer than 2024, while 2.1 billion experienced moderate or severe food insecurity. It reports Africa’s rate easing from 20.3% in 2024 to 20.0% in 2025, against a still very large burden. These are population estimates for 2025, not observations of meals inside individual homes or proof of uniform improvement. The statement also distinguishes food prices from affordability, which depends on income and essential non-food expenses.

nodes.source_refs: ["https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2025/12/ozempic-changing-foods-americans-buy | After discontinuation, the effects become smaller | 2025-12-19"]
nodes.statement: Cornell’s December 19, 2025 account of linked US household transactions and medication surveys reports grocery spending falling 5.3% within six months of GLP-1 adoption and limited-service restaurant spending about 8%. Roughly one-third of users discontinued during the study; spending reverted toward baseline. The authors cannot fully separate appetite suppression from concurrent lifestyle changes. These are household purchases, not measured consumption by each person. The article mentions adoption observations in late 2023–mid-2024 but does not give the full transaction study bounds; it does not establish October 2026 prevalence.

IEA’s 2026 clean-cooking executive summary reports 23% of sub-Saharan Africans had access in 2024: nearly 12 million gained access that year, but population growth left around 14 million more people without it. Its 2025 values are explicitly estimates from early data including stove and fuel imports. This is a measured-access baseline with lag, not verified exclusive everyday use of cleaner stoves.

IEA’s 2026 clean-cooking executive summary reports nearly $740 million of the $2.2 billion pledged at the 2024 summit had been disbursed by end-May 2026. It also reports LPG prices putting fuel beyond many households’ reach in Nigeria and Uganda during the supply crisis. Funding paid out is distinct from commitments, and physical fuel availability from affordability; neither establishes households permanently stopped using smoky fuels.

nodes.statement: USDA FSIS's Leftovers and Food Safety guidance calls for safe initial cooking, prompt refrigeration, rapid cooling in smaller or shallow portions, and disposal of perishable food left at room temperature too long. It gives refrigerated storage of three to four days and describes thermometer-based reheating after microwave thawing. This is handling guidance, not validation of an automated kitchen or a universal guarantee from temperature records alone. Direct retrieval failed with HTTP 403; substantive support comes from the bounded indexed source excerpt. Publication date and update history were not verified.

nodes.evidence_note: YORI demonstrates cooking in a structured setting but explicitly leaves preparation and storage to people. Extending that structure to the receiving and preparation stages is conjectural.
nodes.falsifier: Reliable operation still depends on washed, cut or individually positioned ingredients, or frequent help clearing jams.
nodes.mechanism: Keep the machinery's surroundings predictable while allowing the food to vary. A receiving drawer feeds separate vegetable and raw-animal-food work areas. Cameras and force sensing guide washing, gripping and cutting; fixed tools do difficult operations. Failed grasps are retried, dropped food is isolated, and another ingredient can replace a rejected item. Success requires rejection to remain exceptional rather than a disguised need for human preparation.
nodes.research_question: Can useful ingredient variety coexist with sufficiently few handling failures in a kitchen-sized enclosure?
nodes.scene: Imagined: someone puts muddy carrots and a packet of fish into the receiving drawer, rather than peeling carrots and weighing portions.
nodes.signal: Repeated tests use groceries chosen by independent testers, including unfamiliar shapes, wet surfaces and mixed deliveries.
nodes.statement: By December 2030, enclosed kitchen prototypes repeatedly identify, store, wash and cut mixed deliveries of irregular vegetables, fish and raw meat without residents sorting ingredients into recipe portions or rescuing routine handling failures.
nodes.title: A receiving drawer handles groceries that have not been prepared for a robot

nodes.evidence_note: goodBytz reports automatic pot washing in a commercial installation. That is a partial precedent, not evidence of sanitation across a household grocery-to-meal system.
nodes.falsifier: Fat, starch or scraps accumulate in inaccessible joints, or safe operation needs daily human inspection and scrubbing.
nodes.mechanism: Design food-contact parts for washing from the outset: smooth joints, separated dirty and clean paths, drainable surfaces and cutters that open inside a wash chamber. The kitchen checks wash temperature, flow and detergent delivery, repeats failed cycles and blocks contaminated tools. Tests must cover hidden residue, allergens and raw-to-cooked transfer, not merely visibly clean pans.
nodes.research_question: Can full cleaning fit household limits on water, noise, drainage, space and operating cost?
nodes.scene: Imagined: after preparing fish and vegetables, the cabinet washes its cutting tools and work surfaces while the family eats.
nodes.signal: Independent testing follows hundreds of dirty cooking cycles without technicians dismantling or wiping the equipment between meals.
nodes.statement: By December 2030, enclosed kitchen prototypes automatically clean their cookware, cutters, grippers, receiving areas and drains after varied raw-food meals, with independent residue and microbial tests showing that routine manual scrubbing is unnecessary.
nodes.title: The kitchen removes food residue from every surface it uses

nodes.evidence_note: USDA guidance supports the importance of cooking, cooling and storage history. It does not establish automated tracking. The strongest existing full-cycle household comparator remains unresolved.
nodes.falsifier: Container swaps, uneven cooling or undocumented handling routinely escape detection, or nearly all leftovers must be discarded.
nodes.mechanism: The kitchen automatically portions unserved food into identifiable shallow vessels, measures cooling and storage, and links each later meal to the oldest ingredient it contains. Instrumented serving vessels record time away from refrigeration; opened, mixed or untraceable returns are conservatively rejected. Food-safety testing sets discard rules. Reheating never resets the history or substitutes for safe earlier handling.
nodes.research_question: Can handling records remain trustworthy after food leaves the enclosure, while retaining a useful share of leftovers?
nodes.scene: Imagined: yesterday's untouched lentils become lunch, but an untracked bowl brought home from a party is not accepted for automatic reuse.
nodes.signal: Tests deliberately interrupt cooling, swap containers and return food late; the system blocks unsafe reuse without residents maintaining a log.
nodes.statement: By June 2031, prototype home kitchens preserve a tested identity, ingredient and time-temperature record from cooking through serving, cooling, storage and reheating, and automatically exclude leftovers whose handling record is incomplete or unsafe.
nodes.title: Leftovers keep a handling record instead of relying on a guessed expiry date

nodes.evidence_note: This is a proposed integration milestone. Neither the commercial pot-washing claim nor YORI's controlled cooking demonstrations establish it.
nodes.falsifier: Individually capable modules fail when they share storage, tools and water, or staff quietly maintain trial kitchens between meals.
nodes.mechanism: Combine the receiving, sanitation and food-history prototypes by June 2031, then run successive household trials. One controller schedules refrigeration, cutting, cooking, cooling and washing so that each subsystem cannot quietly hand its unfinished work to a person. Local fault recovery isolates spills and switches to another safe dish. Trials count every physical rescue, technician visit, rejected grocery and missed meal.
nodes.research_question: What failure frequency and maintenance interval survive months of household dirt, interruptions and changing groceries?
nodes.scene: Imagined: the kitchen postpones washing one pot until rice is served, while another chamber chills the unused vegetables.
nodes.signal: Published household logs report total human work and service visits, not only successful cooking demonstrations.
nodes.statement: By December 2032, integrated kitchen prototypes complete six-month occupied-home trials using varied ordinary groceries, including safe leftover reuse, with no routine human ingredient preparation or cleaning of the machinery's food-contact surfaces.
nodes.title: Storage, preparation and washing work together through repeated meals

nodes.evidence_note: Existing evidence establishes space constraints, the price of a partial cooking device and a commercial installation—not a viable household cost. The proposed simplification is unproven.
nodes.falsifier: Required space, electrical work, plumbing or servicing keeps total cost in the luxury market.
nodes.mechanism: Use fixed preparation tools and a compact transfer mechanism rather than several general-purpose arms. Share pumps, insulation and heating parts with appliance production, while keeping dirty and clean food paths separate. Replaceable service modules reduce repair cost. Costing includes installation, water, energy, consumables and maintenance; financing alone cannot make an expensive lifetime cost affordable.
nodes.research_question: Can enough variety and automatic cleaning survive the reductions in size and cost needed for ordinary buyers?
nodes.scene: Imagined: a household compares the installed system with replacing its kitchen cabinets and appliances, rather than commissioning a bespoke robot room.
nodes.signal: An audited bill of materials and installation trials are followed by firm service prices and orders from buyers without exceptional incomes.
nodes.statement: By December 2031, a kitchen manufacturer has a costed, independently reviewed production and repair design for an enclosed grocery-to-meal kitchen that fits ordinary residential utilities and can be financed within a middle-income kitchen-replacement budget in at least one launch market.
nodes.title: The machinery fits a household purchase rather than a luxury demonstration

nodes.evidence_note: This is the unchanged imagined commitment. The route proposes achieving it in 2033 to leave time for the later access and behavior milestones; no present source proves it.
nodes.falsifier: Sold units require routine preparation, daily scrubbing, frequent physical rescue or luxury-level support.
nodes.mechanism: Use the December 2032 household-tested design and December 2031 production plan to begin verified sales and operation by December 2033, ahead of the endpoint deadline. Buyers still supply groceries, utilities and occasional maintenance, but do not wash, chop, portion or clean food-contact machinery as a routine meal task. Installation and service contracts must preserve the tested performance outside supervised trials.
nodes.research_question: Will production units retain prototype reliability at a household price?
nodes.scene: Imagined: a resident requests dinner after putting groceries away through the receiving drawer; there is no chopping board or pan to wash afterward.
nodes.signal: Ordinary paying households reproduce the trial results without technician attendance or prepared ingredient kits.
nodes.statement: By 2035, home kitchens sold to ordinary households can store, prepare and cook varied unpackaged ingredients, then clean themselves without routine human intervention.
nodes.title: Ordinary buyers can hand over the whole fresh-meal cycle

nodes.evidence_note: The original commitment is preserved. Current full-cycle household tracking remains an open comparison; food-safety guidance is a design constraint, not evidence that this capability exists.
nodes.falsifier: The kitchen loses food identity or safety history, or useful reuse depends on residents recording and checking every container.
nodes.mechanism: Deploy the tested food-history system with the first household units by December 2033. Automatic cooling, container identification and recipe selection allow eligible leftovers to replace fresh ingredients while preserving ingredient age and handling limits. Unknown food is rejected rather than made safe by assertion. Trials must show useful reuse, not safety achieved only by discarding everything.
nodes.research_question: How much household leftover food remains eligible once uncertain handling and contamination are treated honestly?
nodes.scene: Imagined: spare cooked vegetables become part of tomorrow's soup without anyone remembering when they entered the fridge.
nodes.signal: Independent tests link reused portions to complete handling records and check both unsafe releases and unnecessary discards.
nodes.statement: By 2035, these kitchens track storage and handling sufficiently to reuse household leftovers safely in subsequent meals.
nodes.title: Yesterday's food safely becomes an ingredient in tomorrow's meal

nodes.evidence_note: This is an unresolved design prerequisite. No supplied or newly retrieved finding validates this complete accessible serving arrangement.
nodes.falsifier: Users can request meals but still need someone to lift cookware, open the serving compartment or make the food safe to touch.
nodes.mechanism: Develop the serving interface alongside the enclosed machinery. Offer physical switches, speech and alternative controls; separate adult setup from everyday meal requests. Locked compartments contain hazardous movement. A height-adjustable serving drawer releases stable dishes only after temperature checks. Testing includes weak grip, seated reach, mistaken requests and interrupted power, rather than assuming speech control solves access.
nodes.research_question: Which ages and mobility needs can be served safely without confusing independent meal access with independent eating or freedom from all care?
nodes.scene: Imagined: a wheelchair user presses a large switch and receives a warm bowl on a tray at their own height.
nodes.signal: People with different mobility limitations and children complete supervised usability and safety tests without a helper touching cooking controls.
nodes.statement: By December 2031, an independently tested kitchen control and serving design lets children and adults with limited mobility request approved meals and receive dishes within reach without exposure to moving blades, hot cookware or dangerously hot food.
nodes.title: A meal request does not require reaching a hot pan or a touchscreen

nodes.evidence_note: This is a proposed household validation step, not an observed benefit of cooking automation.
nodes.falsifier: Apparent independence depends on another person loading portions, resetting faults or retrieving each hot dish.
nodes.mechanism: Install the 2031-tested control and serving design in units sold by December 2033. Follow users for at least six months in 2034, recording missed meals, unsafe requests and occasions when a helper intervenes. Grocery supply and unrelated care may continue, but help operating the meal machinery cannot be hidden in the results.
nodes.research_question: Do safety restrictions leave enough meal choice and reliable access to be useful?
nodes.scene: Imagined: a child selects an adult-approved lunch while their parent works in another room, without asking the parent to handle the oven.
nodes.signal: Observed meal access agrees with device logs and caregiver diaries, including unsuccessful attempts.
nodes.statement: By December 2034, trials of commercially sold automated kitchens show children and adults with limited mobility repeatedly requesting and obtaining varied hot meals without another person operating cooking or serving equipment.
nodes.title: People who cannot operate a stove use the sold kitchen themselves

nodes.evidence_note: This is the unchanged endpoint commitment. Accessible controls and serving remain separate requirements from automatic cooking.
nodes.falsifier: Routine use restores a helper's role at a cooking, fault-recovery or serving step.
nodes.mechanism: Successful 2034 access trials support routine use through 2035, with the same locked cooking enclosure, accessible controls and safe serving drawer. The claim concerns obtaining meals, not every child or every impairment, and not removal of grocery supply, feeding assistance or other care where needed.
nodes.research_question: Which users retain independent access when the system encounters faults or rejects an ingredient?
nodes.scene: Imagined: an adult who cannot safely lift a saucepan obtains a freshly cooked lunch without waiting for someone else to cook.
nodes.signal: Household records show repeated independent meal access rather than occasional demonstrations.
nodes.statement: By 2035, children and adults with limited mobility in equipped homes can obtain varied hot meals without another person operating cooking equipment.
nodes.title: Children and people with limited mobility can obtain hot meals without a cook

nodes.evidence_note: This is a behavioral and reliability hypothesis. Demonstrated machine capability alone does not establish that people use it for weeks or accept its meals.
nodes.falsifier: Taste fatigue, unavailable ingredients, repairs or leftover exceptions repeatedly send residents back to manual preparation.
nodes.mechanism: Follow the units and leftover system available by December 2033 throughout 2034. Menus reuse stocked ingredients, incorporate safe leftovers and switch dishes when an ingredient fails inspection. Common faults recover locally; occasional repairs are scheduled without becoming a standing household task. Record all preparation, service labor, rejected meals and outside food purchases, including households that abandon the system.
nodes.research_question: Will ordinary households accept the available dishes, conservative food rejections and remaining grocery and maintenance chores?
nodes.scene: Imagined: a family realizes its chopping board has stayed in the cupboard for a month, although fresh vegetables and fish still arrive each week.
nodes.signal: Independent diaries and equipment logs agree on complete preparation-free months, with acceptable variety and no shift to meal kits or takeaway hiding failures.
nodes.statement: By December 2034, year-long follow-up of ordinary buyers shows that most participating households repeatedly complete 28-day periods eating varied fresh-ingredient meals from their automated kitchens without manual food preparation or routine cleaning rescues.
nodes.title: Weeks without preparation survive real groceries, preferences and breakdowns

nodes.evidence_note: This is the unchanged endpoint commitment, reached through a proposed household-use test rather than inferred directly from technical demonstrations.
nodes.falsifier: Residents return to regular preparation, or preparation-free weeks mainly consist of bought prepared meals.
nodes.mechanism: The preparation-free periods established in 2034 persist during ordinary use in 2035. Fresh-food handling and useful leftover reuse remove recurring exceptions, while variety and dependable recovery make daily delegation worth retaining. Residents can still cook for pleasure; this outcome requires that manual preparation is no longer necessary to keep eating fresh meals at home.
nodes.research_question: Does the saved effort remain larger than the effort of managing menus, faults, groceries and service?
nodes.scene: Imagined: someone makes a cake on Sunday because they want to, not because the household otherwise lacks dinner.
nodes.signal: Repeat follow-up finds sustained preparation-free periods, including among buyers who were not technology enthusiasts.
nodes.statement: By 2035, households using these kitchens routinely go weeks without manual food preparation, while continuing to eat meals made from fresh ingredients.
nodes.title: Cooking becomes something equipped households can choose not to do

chain.mechanism: Preparation and washing prototypes are ready by December 2030 and the food-history prototype by June 2031. Combine them from June 2031, leaving eighteen months for integration and six-month occupied-home trials. Shared scheduling must prevent storage, contamination and cleaning failures from turning into resident tasks.

The production and repair design is ready in 2031; integration evidence arrives in 2032. During 2033, complete product validation, installation checks and paying-household deployment. The route explicitly requires the frozen 2035 capability to be achieved by December 2033 so later commitments have time to develop. Cost, sanitation or reliability failure blocks the route.

nodes.statement: Stanford's directly fetched repository abstract for the student project MyReactor, published March 16, 2026, reports a tabletop fungal fermentation prototype based on a modified six-quart pressure cooker. It integrates sterilization, sterile inoculation, filtered gas exchange, agitation and extraction. The abstract reports over 200 g of wet biomass per cycle and approximately fourfold higher yield with agitation than static growth. This is a stronger compact-appliance comparator than manual spirulina cultivation, but wet biomass is not measured dietary protein. The inspected abstract does not establish safe consumption, automatic unsafe-batch detection, months of ordinary household use or a one-third dietary share. The embedded full project report was not inspected; growth-trial dates were not stated.

nodes.statement: The directly fetched abstract of a review published December 3, 2025 in Food Science and Biotechnology says fungal-protein nutritional properties vary by strain, substrate and production method. It reports that most reviewed mycoproteins have protein contents and amino-acid profiles comparable to animal proteins, while flagging inadequate sensory characteristics in various strains and insufficient safety information concerning potential allergens and toxicity. This supports neither a blanket rejection nor a blanket assurance of fungal-food safety. Only the abstract and public preview were inspected; the subscription full text was not retrieved. The review does not validate a household growing process or automatic batch-release tests.

observed.claim: A sponsored online survey of 2,000 US adults, June 12–17, 2026, found 31% reported cooking at home much more than a year earlier; 60% planned weekly meals around overlapping ingredients. These are internet-connected adults' self-reports, not measured cooking time or proof of price effects.

IKEA reports 31,339 adults surveyed online in August–September 2025: 40% watched TV while eating with household members; 25% each cited insufficient storage or surface space. Only indexed text was inspected; country coverage, weighting and question context remain unverified.

A December 2025 Posha home review found automated dispensing, heating and stirring but manual chopping, weighing and loading. YORI's September 2025 paper reports successful controlled cooking trials, while retaining pre-portioned ingredients, human recovery from unexpected faults and no storage or cleaning automation. Neither establishes unattended household meal cycles.

FAO's July 21, 2026 statement estimates 645 million people faced hunger in 2025 and 2.1 billion experienced moderate or severe food insecurity. Affordability depends on income and essential non-food expenses as well as prices. These are population estimates, not observations of individual home meals.

Cornell's December 19, 2025 account links starting GLP-1 medication to 5.3% lower household grocery spending within six months; spending moved toward baseline after stopping. Lifestyle changes may contribute. Purchases do not measure individual consumption; full study dates and October 2026 use rates are unknown.

IEA reports 23% cleaner-cooking access in sub-Saharan Africa in 2024: nearly 12m gained access, but 14m more lacked it after population growth. By May 2026, $740m of $2.2bn pledged was paid. Gas prices excluded many Nigerian and Ugandan households despite supplies. Access and funding do not prove exclusive clean-stove use; 2025 figures are early estimates.

HelloFresh reports Q2 2026 currency-adjusted revenue down 8.9% for kits and 8.4% for ready meals, prioritizing margins. Instacart claims broad US/Canada prompt-to-cart access and larger early orders. One reporter tested chat ordering with payment confirmation or cart review. These do not establish market trends, savings or safety; HelloFresh is indexed-only.

GFI's US retail analysis for 2025 reports plant-based meat and seafood units down 11%, conventional units up 1%, and plant-based shreds, chunks and strips up 8%. This advocacy group's selected retail data do not cover all plant-rich diets or global demand and do not establish causes. Publication date is unknown.

commitments.statement: By 2035, home kitchens sold to ordinary households can store, prepare and cook varied unpackaged ingredients, then clean themselves without routine human intervention.

consequences.mechanism: Removing knives and hot-pan handling can let residents request meals without another cook. But accessible controls, safe serving and child protections are additional requirements; cooking automation alone does not establish them.

The whole cycle removes daily preparation and cleanup; safe leftover handling prevents yesterday's food from becoming a recurring manual exception. Frequent jams, cleaning rescues or unsafe storage would restore the need for a resident cook.

signals: Controlled tests showing large flavor differences with identical food and concealed device settings.

criteria.changed_arrangement: Cited present analogue is supported in its actual scope, and the defining commitments specify materially changed capabilities, experiences or causal operation with dependent consequences. Institutional change is not required. Adoption counts when it enables such a change, not merely greater availability or prevalence.
criteria.present_or_adoption_only: The defining mechanism and its claimed capabilities or experiences already exist in the compared setting, or only price, distribution, prevalence, packaging or convenience changes without a consequential difference in what becomes possible or how it works.

criteria.unsupported_analogue: The cited material does not substantiate the claimed present analogue or necessary scope contrast; absence of evidence is not evidence of novelty.

result.instructions:
A world changes what becomes possible or impossible to do or experience, or how the relevant system actually works, with interacting consequences that answer the user's question. Social or economic arrangements matter when they change those capabilities, experiences or causal operation; they are not required. A new tool, process or medium can be a defining mechanism when its capabilities change the whole answer. Renaming a device, adding decorative scenes or changing ownership does not by itself establish a consequential change. Distinct worlds may share tools or institutions while producing materially different capabilities, experiences and causal paths.

Challenge the chosen analogue against ALL supplied source findings: an uncited stronger present match overrides a weak selected comparison. Check each defining commitment against the strongest relevant existing capabilities, experiences and causal mechanisms, including the present frontier rather than only average adoption. A supported example does not establish that it is closest. A currently published report may project future outcomes: its publication and forecast are evidence only of what the source reports, not that the projected arrangement exists. Preserve claim_type, provenance, source_correction, observation dates and textual qualifications; do not classify a projected outcome as a present counterexample. Reported queries are researcher self-report, not independently verified search or proof of absence. If necessary comparison coverage remains unknown, choose unresolved. Preserve scope/date caveats. Do not award novelty for low probability, future dates, narrative length, or unsupported claims about today's absence. A familiar mechanism under changed conditions may qualify if its newly enabled capabilities or consequences are explicit and supported by the present comparison.

result.instructions:
A world changes what becomes possible or impossible to do or experience, or how the relevant system actually works, with interacting consequences that answer the user's question. Social or economic arrangements matter when they change those capabilities, experiences or causal operation; they are not required. A new tool, process or medium can be a defining mechanism when its capabilities change the whole answer. Renaming a device, adding decorative scenes or changing ownership does not by itself establish a consequential change. Distinct worlds may share tools or institutions while producing materially different capabilities, experiences and causal paths.

Challenge the chosen analogue against ALL supplied source findings: an uncited stronger present match overrides a weak selected comparison. Check each defining commitment against the strongest relevant existing capabilities, experiences and causal mechanisms, including the present frontier rather than only average adoption. A supported example does not establish that it is closest. A currently published report may project future outcomes: its publication and forecast are evidence only of what the source reports, not that the projected arrangement exists. Preserve claim_type, provenance, source_correction, observation dates and textual qualifications; do not classify a projected outcome as a present counterexample. Reported queries are researcher self-report, not independently verified search or proof of absence. If necessary comparison coverage remains unknown, choose unresolved. Preserve scope/date caveats. criteria.changed_arrangement: Cited present analogue is supported in its actual scope, and the defining commitments specify materially changed capabilities, experiences or causal operation with dependent consequences. Institutional change is not required. Adoption counts when it enables such a change, not merely greater availability or prevalence.
criteria.present_or_adoption_only: The defining mechanism and its claimed capabilities or experiences already exist in the compared setting, or only price, distribution, prevalence, packaging or convenience changes without a consequential difference in what becomes possible or how it works.
criteria.unresolved: A consequential present-relative change is not established.
criteria.unsupported_analogue: The cited material does not substantiate the claimed present analogue or necessary scope contrast; absence of evidence is not evidence of novelty.

result.instructions:
A world changes what becomes possible or impossible to do or experience, or how the relevant system actually works, with interacting consequences that answer the user's question. Social or economic arrangements matter when they change those capabilities, experiences or causal operation; they are not required. A new tool, process or medium can be a defining mechanism when its capabilities change the whole answer. Renaming a device, adding decorative scenes or changing ownership does not by itself establish a consequential change. Distinct worlds may share tools or institutions while producing materially different capabilities, experiences and causal paths.

Challenge the chosen analogue against ALL supplied source findings: an uncited stronger present match overrides a weak selected comparison. Check each defining commitment against the strongest relevant existing capabilities, experiences and causal mechanisms, including the present frontier rather than only average adoption. A supported example does not establish that it is closest. A currently published report may project future outcomes: its publication and forecast are evidence only of what the source reports, not that the projected arrangement exists. Preserve claim_type, provenance, source_correction, observation dates and textual qualifications; do not classify a projected outcome as a present counterexample. Reported queries are researcher self-report, not independently verified search or proof of absence. If necessary comparison coverage remains unknown, choose unresolved. Preserve scope/date caveats. Do not award novelty for low probability, future dates, narrative length, or unsupported claims about today's absence. A familiar mechanism under changed conditions may qualify if its newly enabled capabilities or consequences are explicit and supported by the present comparison.

observed.claim: A sponsored online survey of 2,000 US adults, June 12–17, 2026, found 31% reported cooking at home much more than a year earlier; 60% planned weekly meals around overlapping ingredients. These are internet-connected adults' self-reports, not measured cooking time or proof of price effects.

IKEA reports 31,339 adults surveyed online in August–September 2025: 40% watched TV while eating with household members; 25% each cited insufficient storage or surface space. Only indexed text was inspected; country coverage, weighting and question context remain unverified.

A December 13, 2025 Posha review found automated dispensing, heating and stirring, but manual chopping, weighing and loading. Meals served 1–4 and took about 30–60 minutes, sometimes longer than manual cooking. The setup cost $1,500 plus about $15/month and needed internet and counter space. This was one review, not population-wide evidence.

FAO's July 21, 2026 statement estimates 645 million people faced hunger in 2025 and 2.1 billion experienced moderate or severe food insecurity. Affordability depends on income and essential non-food expenses as well as prices. These are population estimates, not observations of individual home meals.

Lifestyle changes may contribute. Purchases do not measure individual consumption; full study dates and October 2026 use rates are unknown.

consequences.mechanism: Steady edible output and trustworthy safety could make the culture a routine protein source. Yield, taste, nutrient balance and input costs must also work; a safe vessel alone does not make families eat its output regularly.

Only substantial replacement of purchased protein changes shopping toward feed and culture servicing. Occasional spoonfuls leave the usual refrigerated protein supply largely intact; failed batches still require backup food.

criteria.changed_arrangement: Cited present analogue is supported in its actual scope, and the defining commitments specify materially changed capabilities, experiences or causal operation with dependent consequences. Institutional change is not required. Adoption counts when it enables such a change, not merely greater availability or prevalence.
criteria.present_or_adoption_only: The defining mechanism and its claimed capabilities or experiences already exist in the compared setting, or only price, distribution, prevalence, packaging or convenience changes without a consequential difference in what becomes possible or how it works.
criteria.unresolved: A consequential present-relative change is not established.
criteria.unsupported_analogue: The cited material does not substantiate the claimed present analogue or necessary scope contrast; absence of evidence is not evidence of novelty.

result.instructions:
A world changes what becomes possible or impossible to do or experience, or how the relevant system actually works, with interacting consequences that answer the user's question. Social or economic arrangements matter when they change those capabilities, experiences or causal operation; they are not required. A new tool, process or medium can be a defining mechanism when its capabilities change the whole answer. Renaming a device, adding decorative scenes or changing ownership does not by itself establish a consequential change. Distinct worlds may share tools or institutions while producing materially different capabilities, experiences and causal paths.

Challenge the chosen analogue against ALL supplied source findings: an uncited stronger present match overrides a weak selected comparison. Check each defining commitment against the strongest relevant existing capabilities, experiences and causal mechanisms, including the present frontier rather than only average adoption. A supported example does not establish that it is closest. A currently published report may project future outcomes: its publication and forecast are evidence only of what the source reports, not that the projected arrangement exists. Preserve claim_type, provenance, source_correction, observation dates and textual qualifications; do not classify a projected outcome as a present counterexample. Reported queries are researcher self-report, not independently verified search or proof of absence. If necessary comparison coverage remains unknown, choose unresolved. Preserve scope/date caveats. Do not award novelty for low probability, future dates, narrative length, or unsupported claims about today's absence. A familiar mechanism under changed conditions may qualify if its newly enabled capabilities or consequences are explicit and supported by the present comparison.

analogue.statement: Electrical utensils already alter perceived saltiness: Kirin reported roughly 1.5-times enhancement in tests with people on low-sodium diets. That is a direct precursor to changing experience without adding equivalent ingredients. It does not establish smoky versus herbal dinners from identical food, lasting enjoyment or reduced purchases. Stronger complex-flavor interfaces were sought, but adequate retrieved support for that frontier comparison is missing.

observed.claim: A sponsored online survey of 2,000 US adults, June 12–17, 2026, found 31% reported cooking at home much more than a year earlier; 60% planned weekly meals around overlapping ingredients. These are internet-connected adults' self-reports, not measured cooking time or proof of price effects.

IKEA reports 31,339 adults surveyed online in August–September 2025: 40% watched TV while eating with household members; 25% each cited insufficient storage or surface space. Only indexed text was inspected; country coverage, weighting and question context remain unverified.

A December 13, 2025 Posha review found automated dispensing, heating and stirring, but manual chopping, weighing and loading. Meals served 1–4 and took about 30–60 minutes, sometimes longer than manual cooking. The setup cost $1,500 plus about $15/month and needed internet and counter space. This was one review, not population-wide evidence.

FAO's July 21, 2026 statement estimates 645 million people faced hunger in 2025 and 2.1 billion experienced moderate or severe food insecurity. Affordability depends on income and essential non-food expenses as well as prices. These are population estimates, not observations of individual home meals.

Cornell's December 19, 2025 account links starting GLP-1 medication to 5.3% lower household grocery spending within six months; spending moved toward baseline after stopping. Lifestyle changes may contribute. Purchases do not measure individual consumption; full study dates and October 2026 use rates are unknown.

IEA reports 23% cleaner-cooking access in sub-Saharan Africa in 2024: nearly 12m gained access, but 14m more lacked it after population growth. By May 2026, $740m of $2.2bn pledged was paid. Gas prices excluded many Nigerian and Ugandan households despite supplies. Access and funding do not prove exclusive clean-stove use; 2025 figures are early estimates.

HelloFresh reports Q2 2026 currency-adjusted revenue down 8.9% for kits and 8.4% for ready meals, prioritizing margins. Instacart claims broad US/Canada prompt-to-cart access and larger early orders. One reporter tested chat ordering with payment confirmation or cart review. These do not establish market trends, savings or safety; HelloFresh is indexed-only.

GFI's US retail analysis for 2025 reports plant-based meat and seafood units down 11%, conventional units up 1%, and plant-based shreds, chunks and strips up 8%. This advocacy group's selected retail data do not cover all plant-rich diets or global demand and do not establish causes. Publication date is unknown.

Indexed BLS 2025 data show daily food-preparation/cleanup participation among US people 15+: 65.2% overall, 57.9% men, 72.2% women—not time spent. India's 2024 survey reports 289 daily domestic-work minutes for female participants 6+, versus 88 for males—not cooking alone or all-person averages. Direct retrieval failed for both; publication dates are unverified.

UNEP's March 27, 2024 release estimates 1.05 billion tonnes of retail and consumer food waste in 2022, with 60% in households. It includes inedible parts, not just avoidable leftovers. This is an older modelled estimate, not a 2026 measurement; only indexed text was inspected after direct access failed.

World Happiness Report 2025 uses 2022–2023 self-reports from 142 countries and territories on shared lunches and dinners. Rates differ widely; some Asian respondents may not count household members as 'someone you know.' Meals are not restricted to home, and wellbeing associations do not establish causation.

FSA's 2023–2024 survey of 5,808 adults in England, Wales and Northern Ireland found 12% reported intolerance, 4% allergy and 1% coeliac disease; 76% with hypersensitivity had no diagnosis. Among fridge owners, 58% reported checking temperature. These are self-reports. Published 2024, updated 2025; only indexed text was available after HTTP 410.

Moley's instructions retain human ingredient preparation. Foodini prints loaded fillings; home spirulina instructions require manual harvesting and pH checks. These show partial cooking, shaping and growing, not unattended meal cycles, varied dry-pantry menus or automatic contamination protection. Foodini and spirulina support is indexed-only; dates are unknown.

A 2019 non-randomized remote dietary-care trial used repeated measurements to individualize advice and reported reduced diabetes medication at two years. Kirin's 2022 tests reported electrically enhanced saltiness. Neither establishes automatic family-meal formulation, many convincing flavors or sustained household purchase changes.

Historical Isokon housing linked small kitchens to shared meal preparation; the communal kitchen became a restaurant in 1937. A VideoDining record describes testing video companionship during older adults' meals, not proven replacement of physical help. These are precedents, not verified current district services or remote eating households; support is indexed.

A directly fetched 2023 South African article describes power cuts disrupting cooking and a heat-retaining bag finishing morning-started food for evening meals. It establishes separation of stove use from eating, not representative adoption, safety for every recipe, current outage prevalence or protected shared refrigeration.

unknowns: Evidence on daily meals, purchases and technology use is concentrated in the US; ordinary home eating across other regions and income groups remains poorly covered.
The sources do not adequately describe what people eat, who shares meals, dietary needs, cooking skills or how housing and daily schedules shape eating at home.
Selected products and one subscription company do not establish the reach, cost or reliability of grocery delivery, prepared meals or household cooking automation.
Sources retrieved on October 3, 2026 mix observations from 2022–2026 and undated tests. Retrieval dates do not make older findings current; several publication or observation dates remain unknown.
Full-source checks remain unresolved for the IKEA survey, HelloFresh announcement, BLS table and UNEP release; the supplied findings rely on bounded indexed excerpts.
The evidence does not show how food budgets, kitchen space, unpaid cooking work and access to convenient meals interact within the same households.
Current use and net benefits of shopping assistants and cooking devices are unknown, including preparation, cleanup, subscriptions, mistakes and who can afford them.
Current household use of cleaner fuels, continued use of smoky fuels and the effects of fuel costs are not established by access estimates or funding totals.
The medication study does not establish current use rates or how household purchase changes translate into portions, nutrition or shared meals.
The supplied evidence does not establish current household food-waste amounts or how much could be avoided rather than consisting of inedible parts.
Global meal-sharing questions do not isolate meals at home; differences in whether respondents count household members limit regional comparisons.
India's domestic-work figures do not isolate cooking. The FSA survey does not establish clinical dietary needs. Both additions rely on indexed excerpts after direct retrieval failed.
The added surveys broaden the evidence geographically but do not establish 2026 routines or how meals differ across housing types, incomes and working schedules.
Contrast research also uses historical precedents and undated instructions. Foodini, spirulina and VideoDining checks remain indexed-only; these do not establish current reach or reliability.
Current district meal guarantees, shared residential cooling, industrial food-texture capabilities and rich flavor interfaces remain incompletely compared; some searches failed.
Long-term household trials of complete automation, substantial home-grown protein, sensory substitution and remote assistance replacing physical help remain unverified.

consequences.mechanism: Personal control over the flavor signal could let people eat the same dish differently without separate sauces. A small saltiness shift would not support the much richer dinner experiences described.

Flavor delivered partly through the device could replace some ingredients only if it remains enjoyable in daily use. Abandonment or eating extra salty or sweet foods elsewhere would erase the claimed substitution.

defining_commitments.statement: By 2035, consumer eating devices reliably produce several distinct, convincing flavor experiences from the same physical food during ordinary home meals.
By 2035, sustained household use reduces purchases or consumption of some sugar-, salt- and flavor-heavy foods without equivalent declines in reported meal enjoyment.
By 2035, these effects and comfortable use persist across months of routine eating rather than only in brief demonstrations.
